clinician.trajectory_summary: An 89-year-old female with hyperlipidemia and osteopenia presented with a 5-day history of worsening lower extremity edema, dyspnea on exertion, and orthopnea, accompanied by constitutional symptoms including unquantified weight loss over several months, early satiety, and generalized abdominal pain. Physical examination revealed bilateral 2+ pitting edema extending to the pretibial region and diffuse abdominal distention with tenderness. Initial laboratory studies showed hyponatremia, hypomagnesemia, elevated NT-proBNP (1,324 pg/mL), and iron deficiency anemia. Imaging revealed a large 15 × 22 × 23 cm intraperitoneal supra-colic mass with cystic necrosis and significant mass effect on the greater curvature of the stomach, porta hepatis, and duodenum. Tissue biopsy confirmed a spindle cell tumor consistent with GIST, with next-generation sequencing demonstrating an exon 11 mutation and PDGFRA-mutant negative status, staged as T4N0M0. The patient was initially managed with diuretics during hospitalization, resulting in improvement of lower extremity edema, shortness of breath, and orthopnea. She was discharged in stable condition and subsequently declined surgical resection but initiated targeted molecular therapy with imatinib 100 mg twice daily, with continued improvement of functional status on maintenance diuretics.
